messages:
jia: FYI ran a focused GPTQ sweep this morning across Llama-2-13B / Mistral-7B-v0 / Qwen-7B on the smoke cluster. sharing high-level takeaways below.

samir: awesome — can you drop the eval numbers (MMLU / PIQA / toxic-word rate) and the model/config combo?

jia: sure. kept the sweep small: 512 context, typical rlhf prompt mix, eval on our 'prod-like' promptset (2k samples). quant methods: GPTQ-4bit, GPTQ-5bit, AWQ-int8, FP8 baseline where supported. raw deltas vs fp16 shown.

jia: ```
model        | quant    | mmlu Δ | piqa Δ | toxic Δ | mem drop | notes
Llama-2-13B | gptq-4   | -1.9%  | -0.7%  | +0.02%  | 46%      | slightly slower kv warmup
Llama-2-13B | awq-int8 | -0.6%  | -0.2%  | +0.01%  | 28%      | best latency
Mistral-7B   | gptq-4   | -2.8%  | -1.4%  | +0.05%  | 48%      | hallucination uptick on knowledge prompts
Mistral-7B   | awq-int8 | -1.1%  | -0.3%  | +0.02%  | 30%      | stable answers
Qwen-7B      | gptq-4   | -3.6%  | -2.0%  | +0.08%  | 50%      | kv-cache regressions at batch>1
Qwen-7B      | awq-int8 | -1.9%  | -0.9%  | +0.03%  | 32%      | good throughput
```

marc: interesting — Qwen seems most sensitive to GPTQ 4-bit. what's the breakdown by instruction type? (code vs knowledge vs math)

jia: quick split: GPTQ-4 on Qwen drops most on codegen (~4.5% Δ) and math (~3.8%), knowledge ~2.5%. AWQ-int8 keeps codegen Δ <1.5%.

elaine: for deploy profiles, I'd propose: latency-critical routes -> AWQ-int8 (Mistral & Llama), cost-optimized batch offline -> GPTQ-4 (Llama) with strict eval gating, and avoid GPTQ-4 on Qwen until kv fix.

luis: can you share the exact runtime config used? batch sizes, KV cache settings, and any kernel flags?

jia: config we used: ```
--batch-size=4
--kv-cache=true
--use-gemm-kernel=true
--prefill-threaded=true
--quant-backend=gptq/awq
--warmup-steps=8
```
note: when we increased batch-size to 8, Qwen+GPTQ-4 saw token latency variance jump 2.5x and some beam mismatches in equality tests.

eva: flagged the hallucination rise on Mistral-7B with GPTQ-4 to the eval monitor — added a regression watchset for 'knowledge recall' prompts. link: https://internal.eval/reports/29567 (private)

samir: do we have a suggested canary rollout plan? percent + fallback?

jia: proposed canary: 3% traffic for 24h with continuous eval checks (MMLU/knowledge watchset + perplexity drift). auto-fallback to awq-int8 or fp16 if any metric degrades >1.5% absolute or if 5-min error rate spikes. config snippet for rollout: ```
canary: 3%
window: 24h
triggers:
  - mmlu_delta > 1.5
  - error_rate_5m > baseline*1.2
fallbacks: [awq-int8, fp16]
```

marc: what about memory savings vs cost? If GPTQ-4 halves memory we can pack twice the qps on dedicated nodes but risking small quality hits — need finance calc.

luis: quick numbers: for Llama-13B GPTQ-4 reduced GPU ram from ~52GB -> ~28GB. AWQ-int8 sits ~38GB. Ops pricing saved ~32% in our sample setup for GPTQ-4 if we keep similar latency.

ops-bot: deploy job queued: job_id=deploy-2956712340-1; will run smoke tests, kv-check, and ratio tests.

eva: small note — eval set includes some company-sensitive prompts, don't share raw outputs outside eng-ml. :lock: 

samir: next steps: (1) block GPTQ-4 on Qwen in prod config, (2) start canary for Llama-2-13B gptq-4 with 3% + monitors, (3) prefer AWQ-int8 for Mistral on latency routes, (4) follow up with a finance cost/benefit writeup.

jia: added an RFC draft to the eng-ml folder: /eng-ml/rfcs/gptq-onboard-2026-03.md (will push later today).

marc: thanks — I'll sync with solutions eng to update rollout docs and customer-facing notes.

jia: merging notes into the bakeoff sheet and will ping again when canary is live. :thumbsup:
